# DiskCleaner — Full Reference

> A released, Apple-notarized macOS utility app that scans 16+ cleanup categories, shows every file before it moves, and sends cleaned items to Trash. Free core cleaning is included. Premium is a $9.99 one-time purchase — no subscription.

## What It Does

DiskCleaner scans 16+ cleanup categories and targeted locations on macOS, then shows you every file before moving anything. All cleaned files go to macOS Trash — nothing is permanently deleted.

### Free core cleaning

1. App Cache — per-app cache folders, including the regenerating QuickLook thumbnail cache
2. System Logs — app and system log files
3. Screenshots — Screenshot PNG files accumulated on your Desktop
4. .DS_Store Files — hidden Finder metadata files across your home folder
5. macOS Trash — files still consuming space in your Trash

### Premium cleaning

- Browser Cache — Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Arc, and Opera cache folders
- Developer Data — Xcode DerivedData, CoreSimulator files, and old iOS DeviceSupport files
- Homebrew Cache — stale Homebrew downloads
- Movies — offline downloads and large files in the Movies folder
- Downloads — installers and partial files
- Large Files — files over 50 MB across the home folder
- iOS Backups — old device backups that can consume tens of gigabytes
- Mail Attachments — Apple Mail attachment cache
- App Leftovers — orphaned bundles from uninstalled apps
- External Storage — junk on connected USB drives and external hard drives
- Time Machine Snapshots — local APFS snapshots, always presented for careful review
- Old Installers — DMG and PKG files in Downloads and Desktop

## Special Modules

### App Uninstaller
Cleanly removes apps and all associated leftover files. Supports drag-and-drop from Finder or /Applications. Classifies leftover files by risk level (Safe, Caution, Review) before any removal. Shows every file for review with per-file checkboxes — same review model as cleanup scans.

### RAM Optimizer
Live memory telemetry dashboard. Displays Memory Pressure, Compressed Memory, Swap Used, and Page In/Out metrics in real time. One-tap safe memory optimization using the Apple-approved purge path. Shows the difference between what macOS reports as "used" vs what is actually freeable.

### Large Files Scanner
Surfaces files over 50 MB across the home folder. Displays file name, path, size, and last-accessed date. Per-file review before any action. Available with Premium.

### Menu Bar App
Quick disk usage overview accessible from the Mac's menu bar at all times. Shows free space, triggers scans, and displays update badges without opening the main app.

### Sparkle Auto-Updates
DiskCleaner uses Sparkle for background update delivery, with a secure update feed and signature verification support. Users can still download the latest DMG directly from the website.

## Safety Model

DiskCleaner never permanently deletes files. Every item moved goes to macOS Trash, where it can be reviewed and recovered. Users see a complete checklist of every file before anything is moved. Protected system paths, iCloud sync folders, and app data are blocked from deletion. Risky and personal findings are never pre-selected.

## Risk Classification

Leftover files and cleanup candidates are classified into three categories:
- Safe — commonly safe to remove (e.g., cache, derived data, old logs)
- Caution — potentially useful files that the user should verify before removing
- Review — files that warrant manual review due to unusual location or size

## Permissions

DiskCleaner requests Full Disk Access and Home Folder access from macOS to enable comprehensive scanning. These permissions are optional — scans run at reduced scope without them. Finder Automation is used for Trash operations. No permission data is transmitted anywhere.

## Pricing

- Free tier: App Cache, System Logs, Screenshots, .DS_Store files, and macOS Trash cleaning with no scan limit
- Pro: $9.99 one-time purchase
  - Covers up to 2 Macs
  - Includes all future updates
  - No subscription, no renewal, no upsells
  - License managed via the app (no account creation required)

## Compatibility

- macOS 13 Ventura
- macOS 14 Sonoma
- macOS 15 Sequoia
- macOS 26 Tahoe
- Universal Binary: native Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) and Intel

## Privacy

- No internet connection required for scanning or cleaning
- No analytics, tracking, or telemetry in the app
- No account registration
- No background network calls for scanning or cleaning. Sparkle handles background app updates without transmitting scan results or file data.
- File names, paths, and disk contents never leave the machine

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is DiskCleaner safe?
A: Yes. No file is ever permanently deleted. Everything goes to macOS Trash and is recoverable. You review every file before anything moves.

Q: What is included for free?
A: Core cleaning for App Cache, System Logs, Screenshots, .DS_Store files, and macOS Trash is available without upgrading. A one-time $9.99 Premium purchase unlocks the full scanner for up to 2 Macs including all future updates — no subscription.

Q: Does DiskCleaner collect my data or make background network calls?
A: Scanning and cleanup run locally. DiskCleaner does not collect telemetry, and your file names and disk contents never leave your machine. Sparkle handles background app updates without transmitting scan results.

Q: What macOS versions are supported?
A: macOS 13 Ventura through macOS 26 Tahoe. Universal Binary for Apple Silicon and Intel.

Q: Is there a subscription?
A: No. $9.99 one-time purchase covers up to 2 Macs and includes all future updates — no subscription, no renewal, no upsells.

Q: How is it different from other Mac cleaners?
A: Most cleaners delete files silently. DiskCleaner shows you every single file first, with per-file checkboxes, and only moves files to Trash — never permanent deletion.

Q: What is included for free and what does Premium unlock?
A: Free core cleaning covers App Cache, System Logs, Screenshots, .DS_Store files, and macOS Trash. Premium unlocks the full 16+ category scanner, including browser cache, developer data, Homebrew downloads, large files, backups, external storage, local Time Machine snapshots, and old installers.

Q: Does DiskCleaner require Full Disk Access?
A: Full Disk Access and Home Folder permissions are requested to enable comprehensive scanning. Scans work at reduced scope without them — DiskCleaner never demands access it doesn't have a specific use for.

Q: Does DiskCleaner clean Xcode derived data and iOS Simulators?
A: Yes. Developer Data covers Xcode DerivedData, CoreSimulator files, and old iOS DeviceSupport files.

Q: Can I get a refund?
A: Yes. If purchased through the Mac App Store, Apple's standard 14-day refund policy applies. For direct purchases, contact customersupport@diskcleaner.pro.
